title: Build the engram binary in the review-integrity CI workflow before running the launcher tests
outcome: The GitHub "Review integrity helper" workflow passes on ubuntu, macOS and Windows because it builds the engram binary that the launcher's committed-input tests call
acceptance: `.github/workflows/review-freeze.yml` installs the Rust toolchain and builds `target/debug/engram` (as the launcher tests expect) before `node --test scripts/review-freeze-fingerprint.test.mjs scripts/test-launcher.test.mjs`, reusing the same toolchain and cache actions as ci.yml.

From a clean checkout of the candidate, running the workflow's steps in order (`cargo build --bin engram`, then the two node test commands) passes on a host, with no test skipped, loosened or deleted.
The local full gate is unchanged.

completion.summary: Built Engram before review-integrity CI's existing Node suite; landed the reviewed CI contribution with the shared source-reader candidate and installed the exact gated build. Windows workflow steps and combined full gate passed; six live stores ready. Platform-specific cases accounted for under Greg's clarification.
